title: Variant Admission Orchestra: policy compiler for staged rollouts, probes, and auto-failsafe
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a policy compiler + runtime (the 'Orchestra') that codifies staged variant admission for model rollouts and A/B experiments. The Orchestra accepts declarative route-level manifests describing step schedules, traffic split matrices, shadow probe configurations, health predicates (latency, error rate, quality metrics), and automatic rollback/fallback actions. Goals: 1) provide a compact, composable DSL for product teams to express multi-stage rollouts and experiments; 2) compile DSL -> runtime plans that the serving layer can enact with minimal runtime coordination; 3) implement safety envelopes (hard limits, SLA-aware throttles, cooldown windows) and a shadow probing primitive for non-disruptive verification; 4) integrate with Console telemetry and the Optimize toolkit to suggest step sizes and quantization-aware variants. Deliverables: DSL spec, compiler proof-of-concept, runtime operator library, end-to-end e2e test harness, dashboard hooks for per-step telemetry and rollback controls.
comments: 2026-02-18 - Aisha: Kickoff doc posted (Confluence) describing initial DSL primitives and example staged rollout manifests. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ML/Variant+Admission+Orchestra

2026-02-22 - Miguel: Spike complete - compiled representation is a directed timeline graph (nodes=steps, edges=guards). Prototype compiles into a JSON execution plan and a small runtime evaluator in Go. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestra/pull/12

2026-02-24 - Eng sync: Decided to model shadow probes as first-class actions with a 'probe-budget' token bucket to limit cost during long experiments. Trade-off: extra complexity vs safer verification for models with subtle regressions.

2026-02-27 - Design review: UX asked for explicit per-step explanation strings and telemetry chart anchors to make rollouts transparent in Console; added 'step_description' metadata in DSL. Design doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/designs/orchestra-v1.pdf

2026-02-28 - PM feedback: Require automatic SLA-aware throttling: when cohort latency exceeds threshold for >2m, throttle step growth by halving planned traffic and notify on-call. Added as a compiler-transformed guard.

2026-03-01 - QA: Began writing e2e scenarios. Focus areas: (1) rapid rollback on quality regression (synthetic eval failure), (2) shadow probe detection of perf regressions without user impact, (3) A/B metric tagging continuity when traffic splits change. Test plan draft: https://docs.redwood.ai/orchestra/tests/plan.md

2026-03-01 - Infra note: Runtime will persist plan checkpoints to datastores that exist in Dedicated and Private; for Hosted API we will use ephemeral checkpoints with leader election. Need follow-up to enumerate storage contracts.
Open: Investigate storing long-running probe results in Optimize so suggestions can be correlated with prior rollouts for automated recommendations.
